topic_candidates.title: How Drone Delivery Actually Gets Food to Your Door
topic_candidates.query: Uber Eats Zipline drone delivery Houston how autonomous delivery works November 2026
topic_candidates.brief: Use the viral food-by-drone demo to explain the complete delivery chain: the order is dispatched, the aircraft follows an automated route, avoids obstacles, reaches a safe drop zone and lowers the package without landing. Then explain what still limits the idea—payload weight, weather, noise, airspace rules, battery range and whether homes have a safe handoff location. The angle is whether drones replace delivery cars for small orders, not whether one launch means every meal will arrive by air.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Uber announced a partnership with Zipline to bring autonomous drone delivery to Uber Eats customers, and major reporting described the first commercial service launching in the Houston area in November 2026. Official drone-technology material explains obstacle detection, routing and delivery-zone checks. The video should distinguish a limited commercial rollout from nationwide availability.
topic_candidates.science_angle: Autonomous navigation, computer vision, battery-energy limits, aircraft control, payload design and the regulation of low-altitude airspace.

topic_candidates.title: Dario Amodei: Why Claude’s Creator Worries About AI
topic_candidates.query: Dario Amodei Anthropic AI safety responsible scaling policy why AI labs need safeguards
topic_candidates.brief: Explain why a leading AI builder can be both aggressively pro-AI progress and worried about what more capable systems could do. The story should define the practical risks in plain English—misuse, cyberattacks, loss of control and systems acting beyond the user's intent—then show how evaluations, access limits, monitoring and staged deployment are supposed to reduce them. The conclusion should separate documented safety policies from dramatic claims that an AI is already conscious or rogue.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Anthropic identifies Dario Amodei as its CEO and describes its focus on building reliable, interpretable and steerable systems. Its Responsible Scaling Policy says more capable models bring both benefits and new risks and sets out stronger safeguards as capabilities increase. These sources support a balanced explanation of why AI safety is treated as an engineering and governance problem, not proof of an imminent catastrophe.
topic_candidates.science_angle: AI alignment, capability evaluations, threat modeling, human feedback, interpretability and risk-based deployment controls.
